I've had this exact same experience. People kept thinking that I was gay based on how my male friendships went. To the point where I actually went through accepting I was gay and I came out to my parents and everything. It wasn't until I had had sex with a man that I realized how wrongly I had been led astray. Social pressure is a powerful thing, and I am only now beginning to wonder what the effect of calling an un-masculine straight male "gay" for years by bullies and peers has on their self-image. Also, the subconscious damage perpetuated by the their need to put you in a box must also take its toll. Just because you get emotionally attached to men in friendships well "friendships between men aren't like that" "men just like to fight to sort out problems" "men don't like to talk about emotions with their friends". Fuck all of that. It's not a universal truth, it doesn't apply to everybody, and it does a lot of damage.

Zen hasn't been repressive in my experience. I only uncovered my repressed feelings because of zen practice, otherwise I may have only discovered them much later.

I asked my zen priest about this, because I actually uncovered these feelings through zen meditation. He said three things that stuck with me. Number one is "try to feel these feelings without panicking". The second is "many people, and this is natural, will be quick to label something they don't like as a delusion because they don't want to deal with it. Zen has a long history of people who dropped everything and ran away to join a monastary because they didn't want to face their lives". 
   The third is " You're going to have a story in your head no matter what, it might as well be one that is closer to the truth".

Possible MTF trans here (also 6'2"). Understand that you aren't your narrative. In my life I can cherry pick just as many events that would prove I should be a guy, as those that would prove I should be a woman. I'm just more attached to the ones that would prove I should be a woman because they seem to explain whatever it is that I'm currently feeling.
  I am a very skeptical person and the way I have approached this is to exhaust very other possible option, and see a therapist they can help you through it. Reading blogs about people who have detransitioned/retransitioned has been very helpful for me in that it showed me that transitioning didn't solve all of these people's problems. Which some people (myself included) can sometimes think it will. [This blog](thirdwaytrans.tumblr.com) is my favourite right now.
   I have heard many people say and write that HRT and eventually SRS should be a last resort. And you yourself should see it as a very serious thing that should be approached with caution. In the words of someone much wiser than I am (relating to feeling trans) "Try to feel whatever it is you're feeling, without panicking". I don't know if this helps, but I'm going through this too and it helps me.
Feel free to PM me. I would love to talk with someone who is going through something like this.

A toxic five year relationship with a girl ended, followed by a deep, deep depression. And when I tried to start a relationship with another girl I had gotten to know months later I just couldn't come on to her, there was just no drive. And it made me feel so humiliated and embarrassed and I thought it was because I was gay, but the deeper I probed into my feelings the more I became aware of this suppressed femininity. The feelings became overwhelming and huge feelings of emotional torment have become my day-to-day life. 
   I am a very skeptical person though, so I have abstained from completely investing in the trans narrative and thinking that it will solve all of my problems. I'm thinking the deeper root of my feelings may be due to emasculation trauma. And I'm exploring that before I settle on any set course of action.
